title: Nyamwezi Dried Meat
community: Nyamwezi people of Tabora — the preserved meat of the great traders
author: Mama Salima
desc: Nyamwezi Dried Meat — beef thinly sliced, salted, and sun-dried for 2 days in the Nyamwezi tradition. The preserved protein that fuelled the great caravan journeys from Tabora to the coast — lightweight, long-lasting, and intensely flavoured.
longDesc: Nyamwezi dried meat is the original travel food of Tanzania's interior — thinly sliced beef dried in the sun for 2 days produces a lightweight, highly concentrated protein that keeps for weeks without refrigeration. The Nyamwezi traders who carried ivory and copper hundreds of kilometres to the coast ate this dried meat throughout their journey.
ingredients: 1 kg beef — lean cuts (topside or rump), sliced 3—4mm thin
equipment: Drying rack or clean rope in full sun
steps: Slice beef very thin (3—4mm) against the grain.
Rub each slice with coarse salt on both sides.
Hang slices on a rack or rope in full direct sunlight.
Dry for 2 days in hot sun. Bring in at night.
The meat is ready when completely dry, dark, and rigid.
Store in a clean dry cloth or container.
To eat: eat as is, or reconstitute in a stew.
chefTips: Slice thinly and against the grain — dries faster and more evenly.
Full sun is essential — partial shade produces uneven drying and possible spoilage.
Add the dried meat to stews directly — it reconstitutes beautifully.
cookingScience: See TZA075 for sun-drying science. The Nyamwezi tradition adds no spices beyond salt — the simplicity was intentional for caravan travel where weight and simplicity were paramount.
sustainabilityTips: Sun-drying uses only solar energy — the most sustainable preservation method available.
storage: Room temperature in a dry place for 2—3 weeks. Refrigerate for longer.
culturalNote: Nyamwezi dried meat is the food of the great journeys — the preserved protein that made the East African caravan trade possible. Without this food technology, the Nyamwezi could not have walked hundreds of kilometres across Tanzania's interior. It is the taste of ambition and endurance.
